# `get_device_state`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Read selected sections of the device state (device, settings, camera, focuser, network, storage, sensors, mount, client).

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xf2b80 (64-bit build), handler @0x87720 (32-bit build, section order); station ns_net::pi_station_state, storage FormatStorage, mount GetMountMoveType @0x1814ec, GetScopeAltAz @0x183f6c, GetTrackState @0x186288 (10000 ms waits), GetEqMode @0x17c170 (64-bit build) |

Optional object with keys, a list of section names. Only string elements are kept; a missing or non-object params, a missing or non-array keys, or a list with no strings selects all sections, with no error reply. Failures of one section omit that section and never produce an error reply. The focuser section can open and close the focuser during the query, so its reported state is the state during the query. An all-sections call also issues sequential peer queries with a 10,000 ms wait each, so there is no single bound for the whole request. The setting section is identical to get_setting. Effects differ per key (64-bit build, READ). Client alone is a pure getter; camera and location_lon_lat refresh shared software caches; focuser opens and closes hardware. station, storage and mount only query state and change nothing. station runs a shell query of the Wi-Fi station state, storage reads the cached storage state and file-system usage, and mount sends three read-only queries to the mount controller (moving state, axis coordinates, track state), each with its own 10 s wait, so that section alone can delay the reply by about 30 s when the mount does not answer. No section moves hardware. Sections appear in a fixed order, independent of the order of keys and the same in both builds (device, setting, location_lon_lat, camera, focuser, ap, station, storage, balance_sensor, compass_sensor, mount, pi_status, client). Clients SHOULD still look sections up by name. The method-level tier stays C.

Side effects: Focuser queries may open and close hardware; camera, location, AP and settings paths refresh shared state; the device block runs shell queries and hardware helpers. station, storage and mount are read-only (mount can wait about 30 s). Narrowed selectors differ greatly in effect.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"get_device_state"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object | no | - | Optional. Non-object params and malformed keys are not rejected; they select every section. There is no positional array form. [READ] |
| `params.keys` | array<string> | no | - | Section selectors, case-sensitive: device, setting, location_lon_lat, camera, focuser, ap, station, storage, balance_sensor, compass_sensor, mount, pi_status, client. Duplicates are harmless; unknown strings select nothing. Non-string elements are skipped. Empty, absent or wrong-typed keys selects every section. The order of keys does not affect the reply order. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (error) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Firmware 9.31 has no handler-level error branch. Firmware 9.75 (64-bit) returns an error reply only when encoding the ap password really fails (codes 571 to 573, see the secure-communication chapter); without a crypto session the ap section omits passwd and the call succeeds. Catastrophic helper failures have no established reply shape.

## Example

Request, request - Balance sensor only:

```json
{"id":151,"method":"get_device_state","params":{"keys":["balance_sensor"]}}
```

Request, all - Empty object selects all sections (shape OBSERVED from the iOS app 2026-10-12; values invented):

```json
{"id":152,"method":"get_device_state","params":{}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_device_state","result":{"balance_sensor":{"code":0,"data":{"x":0.01,"y":-0.02,"z":0.99,"angle":1.2}}},"code":0,"id":151}
```

Reply, empty - keys [client] over the tunnel path returned an empty result object (OBSERVED 2026-10-12; guest mode off is INFERRED):

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_device_state","result":{},"code":0,"id":153}
```
